title: The Barbecue (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth Australia Zimbabwe
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The barbecue is a democratic institution in Western Australia
Where everyone stands near the heat and offers up their failure
To resist the urge to turn the meat before it's ready
The barbecue requires patience and a hand both firm and steady

[Pre-Chorus]
Every man within fifteen metres believes he knows the better way
To cook the sausage — this is simply how barbecues operate

[Chorus]
The barbecue knows something I don't know
It knows the exact temperature of showing off the full show
The barbecue is where the men stand and discuss what's on the grill
And nobody moves from their position with sufficient skill
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's always a debate about the equipment and the fuel
And whether the direct heat or the indirect approach is cool
I've been to barbecues where the host explained for forty minutes
The thermometer and its implications before the cooking starts

[Bridge]
In Zimbabwe we cooked on braai over the marula wood
And it took three hours and everything was understood
Without a thermometer — just the colour of the flame
A Perth barbecue is the same idea with different claim

[Outro]
Barbecue knows… the smoke tells everything… barbecue knows
That's my boy
